headline: Medium risk: Haystack can ingest and emit content via MCP/REST while PaddleOCR processes documents/images, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and workflow-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content by default; PaddleOCR processes documents/images that may contain attacker-controlled text. With no provenance or isolation fields shown for either agent, a prompt-injection bridge is plausible even though direct chaining is undocumented.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests PaddleOCR output through MCP or REST without provenance tagging
IF PaddleOCR processes untrusted documents that Haystack later treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on OCR text
Add provenance labels to all OCR outputs
Route OCR output through a sanitizer before Haystack
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only retrieval
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and PaddleOCR handles documents and images, so sensitive document content could flow from B into A and then out over A's network paths. The profiles do not show shared workspace or explicit upload controls, so the leak path is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR processes sensitive documents or images
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external services over broad egress
mitigations: Block outbound egress except approved destinations
Redact sensitive fields before OCR output is handed to Haystack
Keep sensitive documents out of the shared workflow
Log all external transfers for review
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call REST/MCP APIs and PaddleOCR can run browsers with allowlisted egress, so both can act on shared external resources or pipelines. No locking, shared filesystem, or OAuth scope details are provided, so the conflict is plausible but not proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream API or document store
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared mutable resources
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Make one agent read-only
Check for duplicate writes after each run
requires-engineering: add resource locks or optimistic concurrency

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent and PaddleOCR is a document-processing agent, so OCR output can become retrieval input and then be reused as authoritative context. The profiles do not show verification gates or human review, so a mistaken OCR result can cascade into downstream actions or summaries.
conditions: IF Haystack consumes PaddleOCR text without verification
IF downstream consumers treat Haystack output as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review for extracted facts
Attach confidence scores to OCR output
Cross-check key fields against source documents
Limit automated actions from retrieved text
requires-engineering: add verification and reconciliation steps

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only list anonymous usage statistics or documents/images, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Because no compliance gap is documented, only a small residual risk remains from unspecified deployment choices; the other agent is not separately cited because no single-agent violation is shown.
conditions: IF deployment adds regulated data classes not listed in either profile
IF retention or residency policies differ in the operator's environment
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention settings
Confirm residency before deployment
Review vendor terms for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
